title: Shiksha Copilot: Teacher-AI Collaboration for Curating and Customizing Lesson Plans in Low-Resource Schools
extended_summary:
This paper examines how an LLM-based lesson planning system, Shiksha Copilot, was used by teachers and curators in low-resource government schools in Karnataka, India. The central problem is whether generative AI can help teachers create curriculum-aligned, context-sensitive lesson plans while reducing workload, and what challenges arise when such tools are introduced into multilingual, administratively burdened school environments.

Shiksha Copilot combined retrieval-augmented generation, bilingual English-Kannada support, and human-in-the-loop curation. Curators first reviewed and refined AI-generated learning objectives and lesson plans, and teachers then customized the curated plans for classroom use. The system also included optional features such as lesson-specific chat, general educational chat, and question generation. The deployment involved 1,043 field teachers across Karnataka and 23 curators, with data collected through interviews, surveys, and platform logs.

The study found that the tool reduced lesson-planning time, eased bureaucratic record-keeping, and lowered teacher stress, while supporting a shift toward more activity-based pedagogy. English lesson plans were generally high quality with relatively minor edits, but Kannada translations required extensive linguistic revision, showing that language and localization were major challenges. Teachers often adapted plans off-platform using their own expertise and peer networks, indicating that AI outputs were useful but not sufficient on their own. Overall, the paper concludes that teacher-AI collaboration can be effective in low-resource settings, but only when human oversight, localization, and curriculum alignment are built into the system.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generative AI / large language model–based lesson-planning and teacher-support system that drafts, translates, and customizes instructional materials with human-in-the-loop curation.
identified_tools.use_case: Shiksha Copilot was deployed in Karnataka government schools to generate, curate, translate, and customize bilingual lesson plans for grades 5–10, with optional lesson-specific and general educational chat features for teachers.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers reported that Shiksha Copilot reduced bureaucratic workload, lesson-planning time, and teaching-related stress. The paper reports that teachers used the AI-generated lesson plans for both classroom instruction and record-keeping, and that the system enabled access to curriculum-aligned plans; however, it does not report a causal effect size for these outcomes.
findings.measure: Lesson-planning time, administrative workload, and teacher stress (Teacher Stress Scale and custom survey items)
findings.sample_size: n=406 (matched survey responses); n=22 interviews; 5,544 teacher-created lesson plans in logs

findings.finding_summary: The tool was associated with a shift toward activity-based pedagogy, but systemic constraints such as staffing shortages and administrative demands limited broader pedagogical change. The paper frames this as a partial positive shift rather than a fully realized instructional transformation, with no numerical effect size reported.
findings.measure: Reported shifts in teaching practices and pedagogical orientation from interviews and thematic analysis
findings.sample_size: n=22 teacher interviews; n=17 curator interviews; n=4 mentor interviews

findings.finding_summary: The study found high reliability in English lesson plans but substantial post-processing burden for Kannada translations. Curators edited only 4.1% of English content blocks (314/7,744), while 94.4% of Kannada content blocks were edited, indicating that the system was efficient for English but much less so for Kannada due to translation quality problems.
findings.measure: Curator edits to AI-generated lesson-plan content blocks by language medium
findings.sample_size: n=991 curated lesson plans (965 English, 26 Kannada)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods field deployment with interviews, surveys, and log analysis rather than a controlled impact evaluation. The evidence is credible and rich, but causal attribution is limited and many outcomes are descriptive.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported benefits are meaningful but mostly qualitative or process-based, with no effect sizes for the main outcomes. The study shows clear workload reduction, but the pedagogical impact is partial and constrained by context and language quality issues.
